diwarnawt: diwarnawd (diwrnod) — a day; noun m., used adverbially, 'one day' (Val yd oed Wydyon diwarnawt yn y wely 'as Gwydion was in bed one day'); no mutation; final -t = /d/
kyny: kyny (cynnid, obsolete) — although not, even though not; conjunction, kyt 'though' + ny 'not', taking the subjunctive (Kyny bei uchel hi 'though it was not loud'); the b of bei is unmutated after ny; the reading as kyt + ny is an inference
hegyr: egori (agor, agori) — to open; 3 sg. present or impersonal 'opens, is opened' (ual y hegyr 'as it opens', the subject being the chest); h- is a prothetic h before the vowel after the particle y, not a mutation; whether it is active or impersonal is uncertain
rwyuaw: rhwyfo (rhwyfo) — to row, to move the limbs about, flail; verbal noun after progressive yn (yn rwyuaw y ureicheu 'moving his arms about', lit. 'rowing'); rw- written for rhw-, no mutation
ureicheu: braich (braich) — arm; noun f., plural breicheu (breichiau); soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (y ureicheu 'his arms')
blyc: plyc (plyg) — fold, bend; noun m. (o blyc y llen 'from the fold of the cloth'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the preposition o 'from'
guascaru: gwascaru (gwasgaru) — to spread out, scatter; verbal noun, gu- = gw- (yn y guascaru 'and in spreading it out'); radical where y 'his, its' would soften g; the mutation is not shown and the sense of y is uncertain
gwydat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'knew' in -at (lle y gwydat bot gwreic 'a place where he knew there was a woman'); radical after the relative particle y
bronneu: bron (bron) — breast; noun f., plural bronneu (bronnau) (gwreic a bronneu genti 'a woman with breasts with her', i.e. a nursing woman); radical after a 'with'
ymobryn: ymobryn (obsolete) — to bargain, make terms, come to an arrangement (ym- + obryn 'payment, reward'); verbal noun fronted before a wnaeth (ymobryn a wnaeth a'r wreic 'he made terms with the woman'); no mutation; meaning inferred, moderately sure
uagwyt: magu (magu) — to rear, bring up; impersonal preterite 'was reared' in -wyt (Y mab a uagwyt 'the boy was reared'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the particle a following a fronted subject
hof: hoff (hoff) — dear, pleasing; adjective, spelt with single f (hof oed gantunt 'it was pleasing to them'; A hof oed y uab 'and it was pleasing to the boy'); no mutation; reading as hoff is an inference from the construction
synnywys: synnu (synnu) — to wonder, take thought, notice; 3 sg. preterite in -ywys (a synnywys arnaw 'wondered at him, took thought of him'); s does not mutate, the a being the particle; the exact sense of synnu ar is uncertain
ymgeneuinawd: ymgeneuinaw (obsolete) — to make oneself familiar with, become attached to, keep company with; 3 sg. preterite in -awd (a ymgeneuinawd ac ef 'and kept company with him'); no mutation; meaning inferred from context, uncertain
carawd: caru (caru) — to love; 3 sg. preterite 'loved' in -awd (a'y carawd yn uwy noc un dyn 'and loved him more than any man'); radical, the infixed y 'him' after a showing no mutation
pedeirblwyd: pedeirblwyd (pedair blwydd) — four years (old); compound of pedeir (f. 'four') and blwyd 'year'; adjective/noun (yny uu pedeirblwyd 'until he was four years old'); b radical after pedeir
wyth: wyth (wyth) — eight; numeral (y uab wyth mlwyd 'the boy of eight years'); causes nasal mutation of the following noun (blwyd > mlwyd)
mlwyd: blwyd (blwydd) — year (of age); noun f., nasal-mutated (b>m) after wyth 'eight' (wyth mlwyd 'eight years old'; modern wyth mlwydd)
gyuareisket: kyuareisket (obsolete) — apparently an equative 'as big (stout) as' formed on breisc 'stout, bulky' (yn gyuareisket ac ef 'as big as he'); kept as printed, though the form is odd (an equative cyn-breisket is expected); lemma a guess, meaning from context; soft-mutated (k>g) after predicative yn
diwyrnawt: diwarnawd (diwrnod) — a day; noun m., a spelling variant of diwarnawt, used adverbially (A diwyrnawt ef a gerdawd 'and one day he went'); no mutation
raessawu: graessawu (croesawu) — to welcome; verbal noun (y raessawu 'to welcome him'); g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' or after y 'his' standing for the object
gyuarch: kyuarch (cyfarch) — to greet; verbal noun (y gyuarch guell idaw 'to greet him', lit. 'to ask better to him'); soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'to'
kywilydaw: kywilydaw (cywilyddio) — to shame, put to shame; verbal noun (uyg kywilydaw i 'my shaming'); radical in spelling, the nasal mutation after uy 'my' being shown only by the g on uyg
gadw: cadw (cadw) — to keep, hold; verbal noun (a'y gadw yn gyhyt a hynn 'and keeping him so long'); soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'his' standing for the object
gyhyt: kyhyt (cyhyd) — as long; equative of hir 'long' (yn gyhyt a hynn 'as long as this'); soft-mutated (k>g) after adverbial yn
gywilyd: kywilyd (cywilydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m. (Ony byd arnat ti gywilyd uwy 'unless there be more shame on you'); soft-mutated (c>g) as a subject placed after its predicate phrase (arnat ti), the cause being the preceding verb and preposition
dynghaf: tynghu (tyngu) — to swear, decree (a destiny); 1 sg. present/future 'I swear, I will decree' (mi a dynghaf dyghet idaw 'I will decree a destiny for him'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
dyghet: tynghet (tynged) — destiny, fate; noun m., here spelt dyghet without n (the ngh in dynghet below); soft-mutated (t>d) as the object after the verb (dynghaf dyghet 'decree a destiny')
direit: direit (direidd) — wicked, perverse, mischievous; adjective, preceding its noun (direit wreic wyt 'you are a wicked woman'); radical, and it softens the noun after it (gwreic > wreic)
geiff: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present 'will get' (a'r mab a geiff enw 'and the boy will get a name'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative particle a
auar: afar (afar) — grievous, woeful, sorrowful; adjective or noun, here 'woeful' (ac auar arnat 'and woe is on you'); no mutation (vowel); GPC senses uncertain for this use
lit: llid (llid) — anger, wrath; noun m., t for d (drwy y lit 'in anger', lit. 'through the wrath'); radical after the article y
menei: Menai (Menai) — Menai, the strait between Anglesey and the mainland; first part Aber Menei, 'the mouth of the Menai'; radical, genitive-like apposition after aber
guelas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw' (yn y lle y guelas delysc 'at once he saw dulse'); gu- = gw-, radical after the particle y
delysc: dilusg (dylusg) — dulse, edible seaweed; noun m. (delysc a morwyal 'dulse and sea-tangle'); the d is original, so radical, object of guelas
morwyal: morwial (morwial, rare) — a kind of seaweed, sea-rod or tangle (mor 'sea' + gwial 'rod'); noun; meaning inferred from the pairing with delysc; radical after a 'and'
hudaw: hudaw (hudo) — to enchant, work magic on, conjure; verbal noun fronted before a wnaeth (hudaw llong a wnaeth 'he conjured a ship'); radical
guimon: gwimon (gwymon) — seaweed, wrack; noun m., gu- = gw- (o'r guimon a'r delysc 'from the wrack and the dulse'); radical after the article 'r
brithaw: brithaw (brithio) — to variegate, colour, dye in many colours; verbal noun (eu brithaw 'colouring them'; yd oed ef yn brithaw cordwal 'he was colouring leather'); radical after eu 'them'
esgidyeu: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f., plural esgidyeu (esgidiau); radical (esgidyeu llunyaw 'making shoes', the object of the verbal noun)
gwniaw: gwniaw (gwnïo) — to sew, stitch; verbal noun (eu gwniaw 'sewing them'); radical after eu 'them'
harganuot: arganuot (arganfod) — to perceive, see; verbal noun with h- prefixed after y 'their' (y harganuot o'r gaer 'their being seen from the fort'), the h- being the sign of the possessive before a vowel, not a mutation
heilyw: eilyw (obsolete) — form, appearance, aspect (perhaps also colour); noun m. (dwy eu heilyw e hun 'taking away their own appearance'); h- prefixed after eu 'their'; dwy here is a scribal slip for dwyn 'to take, bring', as the log notes; meaning inferred from context
eilyw: eilyw (obsolete) — form, appearance, aspect; noun m. (dodi eilyw arall arnunt 'to put another appearance on them'); radical, object of dodi; meaning inferred from context
adnepit: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; impersonal present subjunctive 'be recognised' in -it (ual nat adnepit 'so that they should not be recognised'); stem with p for b; no mutation after nat (vowel)
dynyon: dyn (dyn) — man, person; plural dynyon (dynion) (Pa dynyon yssyd yn y llong? 'what men are in the ship?'); after pa 'what' the d may be soft-mutated (d>dd, written d) but this cannot be told
doethpwyt: dyuot (dod) — to come; impersonal preterite 'was come, people came' in -pwyt (Yna y doethpwyt 'then they came', lit. 'then it was come'); radical (d) after the particle y
uessur: mesur (mesur) — measure; noun m. (dygwch uessur uyn troet 'bring a measure of my foot'); soft-mutated (m>u) as the object after the imperative dygwch
cryd: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., singular, d written t/d as /ð/ (erchwch y'r cryd 'bid the shoemaker'); radical after the article 'r (masc.)
lunywys: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, form, make; 3 sg. preterite in -ywys (Ynteu a lunywys yr esgidyeu 'and he made the shoes'); soft-mutated (ll>l, written l) after the particle a
ormod: gormod (gormod) — excess; noun/adverb, 'too much, too big' (yr esgidyeu yn ormod 'the shoes too big'); g lost by soft mutation after adverbial yn
ryuawr: ryuawr (rhy fawr) — too big; ry 'too' + mawr 'big', with ry softening m>u (modern rhy fawr, spelt as two words); adjective predicative (Ryuawr yw y rei hynn 'too big are these')
werth: gwerth (gwerth) — value, price, worth; noun m. (Ef a geiff werth y rei hynn 'he will get the price of these'); soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object after geiff
gwnaet: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to make, do; 3 sg. imperative 'let him make' in -et (gwnaet heuyt rei 'let him also make ones'; modern gwnaed); radical at the head of the clause
throet: troet (troed) — foot; noun m., spirant-mutated (t>th) after y 'her' (no'y throet 'than her foot'; yny welhwyf y throet 'until I see her foot'), the possessive being the woman's
hanuon: anuon (anfon) — to send; verbal noun with h- prefixed after y 'their' standing for the object (a'y hanuon idi 'and sending them to her'); the h- is the possessive's sign, not a mutation
dywedwch: dywedut (dweud) — to say, tell; 2 pl. imperative 'say!' in -wch (Dywedwch idaw 'tell him'); radical
lunyaf: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will make' (ny lunyaf esgidyeu idi 'I will not make shoes for her'); ll unmutated after ny (ny mutates only c, p, t, g)
welhwyf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may see' in -hwyf (yny welhwyf y throet 'until I see her foot'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after yny 'until'
uedrut: medru (medru) — to be able, know how, be skilled; 2 sg. preterite 'you were able' in -ut (na uedrut kymedroli esgidyeu 'that you could not fit shoes'); soft-mutated (m>u) after na 'that ... not'
kymedroli: kymedroli (cymedroli) — to moderate, adjust, regulate; verbal noun (kymedroli esgidyeu wrth uessur 'to fit shoes to a measure'); radical after the verb
uedreis: medru (medru) — to be able, hit the mark; 1 sg. preterite 'I was able' in -eis (Na uedreis 'I could not'); soft-mutated (m>u) after na
medraf: medru (medru) — to be able, to hit; 1 sg. present/future 'I shall be able, I shall hit' (Mi a'y medraf weithon 'I can do it now'); radical, the infixed y 'it' after a showing no mutation
dryw: dryw (dryw) — wren; noun m. (llyma y dryw 'behold the wren'); radical after the article y
wwrd: bwrdd (bwrdd) — board, table, ship's side; noun m. (ar wwrd y llog 'on the board of the ship'); soft-mutated (b>u) after ar, spelt with the 6-shaped w (wwrd for uwrd), w standing for /v/
llog: llong (llong) — ship; noun f., a scribal slip llog for llong, the n omitted (ar wwrd y llog 'on the side of the ship'); radical after the article y
uedru: medru (medru) — to hit, strike (with a missile), be able; verbal noun, soft-mutated (m>u) after y 'his' standing for the object (y uwrw a'y uedru 'to throw at him and hit him')
giewyn: giewyn (gewyn) — sinew, tendon; noun m. (y rwg giewyn y esgeir a'r ascwrn 'between the sinew of its leg and the bone'); radical
esgeir: esgair (esgair) — leg, shank; noun f., spelt esgeir (-eir for -air); no mutation after y 'its' before a vowel (y esgeir 'its leg')
chwerthin: chwerthin (chwerthin) — to laugh; verbal noun, radical (Sef a wnaeth hitheu, chwerthin 'and she laughed')
gyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — apparently 'deft, skilful, sure' in the epithet Llaw Gyffes 'deft hand' (ys llaw gyffes 'it is a deft hand'); perhaps the same word as kyffes 'confession' or a separate adjective, meaning uncertain; soft-mutated (c>g) as an adjective after the feminine noun llaw
medrwys: medru (medru) — to hit, be able; 3 sg. preterite 'hit' in -wys (y medrwys y Lleu ef 'he hit him, the Lleu'); radical after the particle y
lleu: Lleu (Lleu) — personal name, 'the fair, bright one', the boy later called Lleu Llaw Gyffes; here with the article y Lleu 'the Lleu'; no mutation (masc. article)
aniolwch: aniolwch (no modern form) — meaning uncertain; perhaps for an diolwch 'our thanks' or diolwch 'thanks' (aniolwch Duw it 'God's thanks to you'?); noun; initial d unexplained; kept as written
llew: Llew (Lleu) — personal name, a spelling of Lleu (Llew Llaw Gyffes yw bellach 'Lleu Llaw Gyffes he is henceforth'); w is the 6-shaped w here; radical
wimon: gwimon (gwymon) — seaweed, wrack; noun m., soft-mutated (gw>w) after predicative/adverbial yn (yn wimon 'into wrack')
chanlynwys: canlyn (canlyn) — to follow, pursue; 3 sg. preterite in -wys (ny chanlynwys ef hwy 'he did not follow it longer'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny 'not'
henbydy: henbydu (obsolete) — apparently 'to fare, prosper, profit'; 2 sg. future in -y (ni henbydy well di 'you will not fare better'); h belongs to the stem; meaning uncertain
ellyngwys: gollwng (gollwng) — to release, let go; 3 sg. preterite 'released, let go' in -wys (yd ellyngwys ef y uab 'he released the boy'); a for o by vowel affection, g lost by soft mutation
dyghaf: tynghu (tyngu) — to swear, decree (a destiny); 1 sg. present/future 'I will decree' (minheu a dyghaf dyghet 'I too will decree a destiny'), spelt without n; soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
gwiscof: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to put on, clothe; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may put on' in -of (yny gwiscof i ymdanaw 'until I put (arms) about him'); radical (gw-) after yny, which does not here soften
handid: handid (obsolete) — in spite of, notwithstanding; particle/preposition (handid o'th direidi di 'in spite of your wickedness'); meaning inferred from context, uncertain
direidi: direidi (direidi) — wickedness, mischief; noun m. (o'th direidi di 'of your wickedness'); written radical d, which may be soft (d>dd) after 'th 'your'
dinllef: Dinllef (Dinlleu, Dinlle) — Dinas Dinlle, the hill-fort on the coast of Arfon, second part of the place-name Dinas Dinllef; radical; the name Dinllef contains lleu/lleuef
allwys: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. preterite 'could' in -wys (yny allwys marchogaeth pob march 'until he could ride every horse'); g lost by soft mutation after yny 'until'
marchogaeth: marchogaeth (marchogaeth) — to ride; verbal noun (allwys marchogaeth 'could ride'); radical
thwf: twf (twf) — growth, stature; noun m. (a thwf 'and growth', in gwbyl o bryt, a thwf, a meint 'complete in form, growth and size'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
alw: galw (galw) — to call; verbal noun, g lost by soft mutation after y 'his' standing for the object (a'y alw attaw 'and he called him to him')
lawenach: llawen (llawen) — glad, cheerful; comparative lawenach 'gladder' (A byd lawenach noc yd wyt 'and be more cheerful than you are'); soft-mutated (ll>l) as the predicate after the imperative byd
aruordir: aruordir (arfordir) — coast, shore-land; noun m. (cymryt yr aruordir 'taking the coast'); radical after the article yr
brynn: bryn (bryn) — hill; noun m., spelt brynn; first part of the hill-name Brynn Aryen, Bryn Arien; radical after a 'to'
aryen: Aryen (Arien) — second part of the hill-name Brynn Aryen (Bryn Arien); exact site uncertain; radical (genitive-like, after a noun)
clutno: Clutno (Clutno) — second part of the place-name y Geuyn Clutno 'the Ridge of Clutno', a ridge on the route to Caer Aranrot; exact site and the nature of the name uncertain; radical
chaer: Caer (Caer) — fortress; first part of Caer Aranrot (Caer Aranrhod), Aranrhod's court on the coast of Arfon; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'to' (parth a Chaer Aranrot 'towards Caer Aranrhod')
amgenu: amgenu (obsolete; cf. amgen 'other') — to change, alter, make different; verbal noun fronted before a wnaethant (amgenu eu pryt a wnaethant 'they changed their appearance'); radical
prudach: prud (prudd) — grave, serious, dignified (MW 'wise, stately'; modern prudd 'sad'); comparative prudach 'more grave, more mature' (yn prudach pryt Gwydyon 'Gwydion's appearance more mature'); p radical, the soft mutation after yn not being shown; meaning uncertain
porthawr: porthawr (porthor) — gatekeeper, porter; noun m. (E porthawr 'O porter'; Y porthawr a aeth 'the porter went'); radical
uorgannwc: Morgannwg (Morgannwg) — Glamorgan, the south-eastern region of Wales; soft-mutated (m>u) after o 'from' (beird o Uorgannwc 'poets from Morgannwg'); final -c = /g/
leuenyd: llywenydd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m., MW lleuenyd (Diruawr leuenyd 'great joy'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr
gyweirwyd: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to prepare, set in order; impersonal preterite 'was prepared' in -wyd (Yr yneuad a gyweirwyd 'the hall was made ready'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
ymadaw: ymadaw (ymadael) — to depart, leave off; verbal noun (amser ymadaw a chyuedach 'time to leave off carousing'); no mutation
gweirwyt: gweiraw (gweirio) — to prepare, set in order (cf. kyweiraw); impersonal preterite 'was prepared' in -wyt (ystauell a gweirwyt udunt 'a chamber was prepared for them'); the g is kept where soft mutation after a would drop it, so the mutation is not shown; meaning inferred from the context and kyweiraw
bylgeint: pylgeint (plygain) — dawn, cockcrow; noun m. (Hir bylgeint 'early dawn', lit. 'long dawn'?); soft-mutated (p>b) after the preceding adjective hir; the phrase meaning is uncertain
gyniweir: geniweir (geniwair) — stir, commotion, bustle (also 'equipment, gear'); noun m., spelt gyniweir (read at high zoom, slightly uncertain per the log) (yd oed gyniweir ac utkyrn a lleuein 'there was commotion and trumpets and cries'); radical; meaning uncertain
lleuein: lleuein (llefain) — crying out, outcry, cries; noun m./verbal noun (utkyrn a lleuein 'trumpets and cries'); radical
gynghan: kynghan (obsolete) — round about, all around; adverb (yn y wlat yn gynghan 'in the land all around'); soft-mutated (k>g) after adverbial yn; meaning from context, uncertain
ydoed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' written with the particle yd joined to it (Pan ydoed y dyd yn dyuot 'when the day was coming'); no mutation
glywynt: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. imperfect 'they heard' in -ynt (wynt a glywynt taraw drws 'they heard the door being struck'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
glywn: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 1 pl. present 'we hear' in -n (ni a glywn utkyrn 'we hear trumpets'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
debygy: tebygu (tybio) — to suppose, imagine, think; 2 sg. present 'you think' (beth a debygy di 'what do you think?'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the relative/interrogative a
chawn: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 pl. future 'we shall get', with a verbal noun 'we shall be able' (ni chawn welet 'we shall not be able to see'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ni 'not'
llyw: llyw (llyw) — helm, rudder, direction, leader; noun m. (llyw y weilgi 'the ... of the sea'); the sense in this phrase (perhaps 'the surface' or 'the course') is uncertain; radical
torr: torr (torr) — belly, bulk, swelling, heap; noun m./f. (ar torr y gilyd 'on the bulk of each other', i.e. heaped one on another); radical after ar; the idiom's sense is from context
allont: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'they may be able' in -ont (yn gyntaf a allont 'as soon as they can'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
chynhal: kynnal (cynnal) — to hold, maintain, defend; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her, it' (the fort, feminine) (a'y chynhal yn oreu 'and to hold it as best'), the y being the possessive standing for the object
allom: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 pl. present subjunctive 'we may be able' in -om (yn oreu a allom 'as best we can'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
chynhelwch: kynnal (cynnal) — to hold, maintain, defend; 2 pl. imperative 'hold!' in -wch (A chynhelwch chwitheu 'and you, hold it'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
keffwch: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 pl. future 'you will get' in -wch (ac yma y keffwch digawn o arueu 'and here you will get enough arms'); radical after the particle y
ymdan: am (am) — about, around; the prepositional base form before a noun, ymdan (gwisc ymdan y gwryanc 'put on about the lad'); obsolete in the modern language, which uses am; no mutation
gwryanc: gwryanc (gŵr ieuanc) — young man, youth (gwr 'man' + ieuanc 'young', contracted); noun m. (gwisc ymdan y gwryanc hwnn 'dress this youth'); radical after the article y
wiscaf: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to put on, clothe; 1 sg. present/future 'I will put on' (a wiscaf ymdanaf inheu 'I shall put (them) on about myself too'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
ymdanaf: am (am) + mi — conjugated preposition 'about me', 1 sg. (ymdanaf inheu 'about myself too'); no mutation
glywaf: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 1 sg. present 'I hear' (Mi a glywaf odorun 'I hear a noise'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
amdan: am (am) — about, around; the prepositional base form amdan (modern am) (wiscaw amdan y gwryanc hwnnw 'dressing that youth'); no mutation
diodwn: meaning uncertain — a verb 'to take off, lay aside' (Diodwn yn arueu weithon 'let us put off our arms now'), 1 pl. imperative in -wn; lemma uncertain (perhaps connected with diosg 'take off'); no mutation shown
ynn: y (i) + ni — conjugated preposition 'to us, for us', spelt ynn (nit reit ynn wrthunt 'we have no need of them'); the same word as in; no mutation
dorri: torri (torri) — to break; verbal noun, soft-mutated (t>d) after y 'to' (y dorri dy dynghetuen 'to break your destiny-oath')
dynghetuen: tynghetuen (tynghedfen) — destiny, fate; a binding oath or decree of fate; noun f. (am dy dynghetuen 'about your destiny'); soft-mutated (t>d) after dy 'your'
bereisti: peri (peri) — to cause, make; 2 sg. preterite 'you caused' in -eisti (y dygyuor a bereisti 'the muster you caused'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative a
dynghet: tynghet (tynged) — destiny, fate; noun m. (a mi a dynghaf dynghet idaw 'and I will decree a destiny for him'); soft-mutated (t>d) as the object after dynghaf
genedyl: kenedyl (cenedl) — kin, race, nation; noun f. (o'r genedyl yssyd ar y dayar honn 'of the race that is on this earth'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article 'r
direidwreic: direidwreic (direidwraig) — wicked woman, mischievous woman; noun f., compound of direit 'wicked' + gwreic 'woman' (direidwreic uuost eiroet 'a wicked woman you have ever been'); radical (the compound is unmutated); uuost is soft after the fronted predicate
hwynteu: hwynteu (hwythau) — they for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Hwynteu a doethant at Math 'they came to Math'); radical
chwynaw: cwynaw (cwyno) — to complain, lament; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a chwynaw yn luttaf 'and complaining most bitterly')
luttaf: llut (no modern form) — grievous, bitter, doleful; superlative luttaf 'most grievously' (yn luttaf yn y byt 'most bitterly in the world'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after adverbial yn; meaning uncertain
paryssei: peri (peri) — to cause, make; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had caused' in -yssei (ual y paryssei yr arueu idaw 'how he had got the arms for him'); radical after the particle y
keisswn: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; 1 pl. present subjunctive/imperative 'let us seek' in -wn (keisswn inheu 'let us too seek'); radical
n: 'n — 'our', the proclitic an contracted after a vowel, the apostrophe half of a'n (oc an hut a'n lledrith 'with our magic and our illusion'); no mutation
blodeu: blodeu (blodau) — flowers; plural of blodeuyn, collective 'blossom' (blodeu y deri 'flowers of the oak'); noun m., radical
deri: derwen (derwen) — oak; deri is its plural 'oaks' (modern deri, collective derw) (blodeu y deri 'blossoms of the oak'); noun f., radical after the article y
banadyl: banadl (banadl) — broom (the plant); noun m. collective, spelt banadyl (blodeu y banadyl 'flowers of the broom'); radical after the article y
erwein: erwain (erwain) — meadowsweet (the plant, Filipendula); noun, spelt erwein (blodeu yr erwein 'flowers of the meadowsweet'); radical after the article yr
asswynaw: aswyno (aswyno, obsolete) — to entreat, beseech, and apparently here 'to conjure up, call forth by magic' (asswynaw yr un uorwyn deccaf 'to conjure the one fairest maiden'); verbal noun; the usual dictionary sense is 'entreat', so this use is uncertain; radical
thelediwaf: telediw (no modern form) — handsome, comely; superlative thelediwaf 'handsomest' (teccaf a thelediwaf 'fairest and handsomest'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
blodeued: Blodeuedd (Blodeuwedd) — personal name, the woman made of flowers for Lleu (blodeu 'flowers'; the second part -wedd 'face, form'); radical, object of dodi (dodi Blodeued arnei 'to put Blodeuedd on her', i.e. to name her)
ossymdeithawc: ossymdeithawc (no modern form) — uncertain: apparently ymdeithawc 'travelling, wandering, itinerant' (from ymdeith 'journey') with an unexplained first part (os-?), or a scribal variant of the Red Book's ossymdeithaw (a verbal noun); in Nyt hawd y wr heb gyuoeth idaw ossymdeithawc 'it is not easy for a man without a realm of his own ... to travel/make his way(?)'; meaning uncertain
gantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', a main division of medieval Wales; noun m., soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (pa gantref yw hwnnw 'what cantref is that?')
dinodig: Dinodig (Dinodig) — Cantref Dinodig, the old cantref of Gwynedd containing Eifionydd and Ardudwy; radical, the name after cantref
eiwynyd: Eiwynyd (Eifionydd) — Eifionydd, the district of Gwynedd on the Llŷn side of the Glaslyn, held to be part of Cantref Dinodig; radical after a 'and'
kyuanhedwys: kyuanhedu (cyfanheddu) — to settle, dwell, make a dwelling; 3 sg. preterite 'settled, established' in -wys (y kyuanhedwys lys idaw 'where he established a court for him'); radical after the relative particle y
mur: mur (mur) — wall; noun m., first part of the place-name Mur Castell (Mur y Castell, usually taken as the Roman fort of Tomen y Mur in Ardudwy); radical
castell: castell (castell) — castle, fortress; noun m., second part of the place-name Mur Castell; radical (the article y is lost in the written name)
gwrthtir: gwrthdir (gwrthdir) — upland, borderland, rough or remote country; noun m., t for d (yg gwrthtir Ardudwy 'in the upland of Ardudwy'); radical after yg (the g being the written trace of yn + gw); sense approximate, uncertain
uodlawn: bodlon (bodlon) — content, pleased, well-disposed; adjective, spelt bodlawn (A phawb a uu uodlawn idaw 'and everyone was content with him'); soft-mutated (b>u) as the predicate after uu

__broaden__.wydyon: Gwydion — personal name (Gwydyon, Wydyon); soft-mutated (G>w) after gan 'with', after e 'to' and in apposition to ynteu (Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion') · also soft-mutated (G>w) as the subject placed directly after the verb (Val yd oed Wydyon diwarnawt yn y wely 'as Gwydion was in bed one day')
__broaden__.gist: kist (cist) — chest; noun f. (ymywn llaw gist 'inside a hand-chest', a small chest); soft-mutated (k>g) as the second element of the compound llaw gist · also soft-mutated after the feminine article y (yn y gist 'in the chest')
__broaden__.kyuuch: kyuuch (cyfuwch) — as high as; equative of uchel 'high' (kyuuch a chrib yr ystauell 'as high as the ridge of the chamber'); no mutation · also 'as loud as', of a sound (Kyny bei uchel hi, kyuuch oed ac y kigleu ef 'though it was not loud, it was loud enough that he heard it')
__broaden__.kigleu: klywet (clywed) — to hear; old 3 sg. preterite 'heard' (a phawb o'r guyrda a'e kigleu 'and every one of the noblemen heard it'); no mutation after a'e 'it' · also after ac y 'as, so that' (kyuuch oed ac y kigleu ef 'it was as loud as he heard it'), the k radical
__broaden__.uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God') · also soft as the object of welei (ef a welei uab bychan 'he saw a small boy'), after interrogative pa (Pa uab 'what son') and after possessive dy/y (dy uab 'your son', y uab 'his son')
__broaden__.lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form · yn y lle 'at once, on the spot' (Ac yn y lle, y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor 'and at once, as soon as he came to the sea'); lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline' · also 'where' as a relative conjunction with y (lle y gwydat bot gwreic 'where he knew there was a woman'); 'in a bad place' (lle drwc yd ym 'we are in a bad place')
__broaden__.ureisket: breisc (breisg) — stout, bulky; equative ureisket 'as stout as' (kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six years'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the equative cyn · also noun 'bulk, stoutness', soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (oed gantunt y ureisket bei dwy ulwyd 'his bulk was pleasing to them, as though he were two years old'), without the equative cyn
__broaden__.dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms') · also a scribal slip for dwyn 'to take away' (dwy eu heilyw e hun a oruc 'he took away their own appearance'; Red Book dôyn)
__broaden__.gallu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m. (herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power'); nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my', written uyg gallu with the g on the possessive · also verb 'to be able', verbal noun after progressive yn (yn gallu e hun kyrchu y llys 'able of himself to go to the court')
__broaden__.hwnn: hwnn (hwn) — 'this' (m.); demonstrative (yr oet hwnn 'this appointment') · also pronoun 'the one that' (namyn yr hwnn a dyly 'but that which it deserves') · also adjective 'this' after its noun (Y mab hwnn 'this boy')
__broaden__.byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag') · also byt 'world', spelt with d (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the world's host of mice'; the Red Book y byt) · also 3 sg. present subjunctive 'there be' after ony 'unless' (Ony byd arnat ti gywilyd 'unless shame be on you')
__broaden__.beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?') · also 'thing' as a noun (ys bychan a beth uyd dy gywilyd 'small is the thing that your shame will be')
__broaden__.pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you') · also interrogative adjective 'what' before a noun (Pwy enw dy uab dy? 'what name has your son?'), no mutation
__broaden__.genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation · also y genhyf 'from me' (yny caffo y genhyf i 'until he gets it from me'), with y 'from' (y gan)
__broaden__.am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one') · also 'because' before na (am na'th elwir y uorwyn 'because you are not called the maiden') and 'on account of' (am y dygyuor a bereisti 'on account of the muster you caused')
__broaden__.elwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (y lle a elwir 'the place that is called'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a · also after na/ni, g lost by soft mutation (na'th elwir 'that you are not called'; ni'th elwir bellach byth yn uorwyn 'you will never again be called a maiden')
__broaden__.gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many') · also 'beside, along' (gan lann y weilgi 'along the shore of the sea'; gan pob llong 'for every ship, by reason of the ships')
__broaden__.lann: glann (glan) — bank, edge, shore; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation (gl>l) after the preposition ar (ar lann y fynnawn 'on the edge of the spring'); not llan 'church, enclosure' · also soft-mutated (gl>l) after gan 'by, along' (gan lann y weilgi 'along the shore of the sea')
__broaden__.arganuot: arganuot (arganfod) — to perceive, discover; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (arganuot y bolyeu crwyn a wnaeth 'perceiving the skin-bags he did') · also verbal noun after y 'their' (Pan wybu ynteu y arganuot o'r gaer 'when he knew their being seen from the fort'), the h- of harganuot being absent
__broaden__.weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object of welsynt (y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith 'where they had never seen work'); gweith 'time' is possible but less likely · also soft after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw weith 'what kind of work') and after y (gohir ar y weith 'delay over the work') · also soft after un 'one' (yn un weith a hynny 'of one make with that') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw weith 'what kind of work')
__broaden__.troet: troed (troed) — foot; noun m., singular (yn y troet 'in the foot'); radical after the article y · also nasal-mutated (t>nh) after uyn 'my' (uessur uyn troet 'a measure of my foot'), the n of the nasal mutation written on the possessive
__broaden__.wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to' · also soft after y 'its' (yn y wneuthur 'in the making of it'), the possessive standing for the object · also softened after dros (dros wneuthur 'instead of doing') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) after a noun that is the subject of the verbal noun (erchwch y'r cryd wneuthur esgidyeu 'bid the shoemaker make shoes')
__broaden__.lawer: llawer (llawer) — many, much; pronoun/noun m. (gan lawer o luossogrwyd 'by many of the multitude'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition gan · also adverbial 'by much, far' after a comparative (yn llei lawer no'y throet 'much less than her foot'), soft-mutated (ll>l) after llei
__broaden__.llaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., in the idiom uch llaw 'above, overlooking' (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also gyr llaw 'beside, next to' (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw 'to sit beside it') · also 'hand' without mutation after the article y (yn y llaw arall 'in the other hand') · also first element of the compound llaw gist 'hand-chest', a small chest (ymywn llaw gist 'inside a small chest') · also in the epithet Llaw Gyffes 'deft hand' (ys llaw gyffes 'it is a deft hand'; Llew Llaw Gyffes), radical
__broaden__.well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land') · also soft as the predicate straight after the verb (nat oed well genti 'it was no better to her') · also na well 'no, not better', reply 'Na well' (soft-mutated gw>w after na) · also 'the better' with henbydy (ni henbydy well di 'you will not fare better'); soft after the verb, as a complement
__broaden__.drydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ymgueiraw a oruc Teirnon ar y drydyd marchawc 'Teirnon made ready as third rider'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (t>d) as a predicate after yn (yn drydyd eur gryd 'as the third gold-shoemaker')
__broaden__.gryd: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker, cobbler; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'from' (gan gryd 'from a shoemaker') · also soft-mutated (c>g) after eur 'gold' as the second part of a compound (eur gryd 'gold shoemaker')
__broaden__.dinas: dinas (dinas) — city, fortified town; noun f. (kyrchu dinas arall 'making for another city'); radical as object after the verbal noun · also first part of the place-name Dinas Dinllef (Dinas Dinlle), the hill-fort near Caernarfon; radical after a
__broaden__.geuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y geuyn attei 'and his back to her') · also in the place-name y Geuyn Clutno 'the Ridge of Clutno', soft-mutated after the article y (cause uncertain, cefn being masculine)
__broaden__.ueirch: march (march) — horse; plural meirch; soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive dy 'your' (dy ueirch 'your horses') · also soft after y 'his' (y ueirch 'his horses') · also soft-mutated (m>u) after ar 'on' (ymgueiraw ar ueirch 'they mounted on horses')
__broaden__.hir: hir (hir) — long; adjective (yn hir 'for a long time') · also the epithet in a name (Hychdwn Hir 'Hychdwn the Tall/Long') · also adjective before a noun, softening it (Hir bylgeint 'early dawn', lit. 'long dawn'(?))
__broaden__.allu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m., softened as the subject after oes (nyt oes allu 'there is no power') · also soft-mutated (g>lost) after y 'his' standing for the object (y hut a'y allu 'his magic and his power')
__broaden__.welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort') · also soft after chawn 'we shall be able' (ni chawn welet 'we shall not be able to see')
__broaden__.wnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall make' (ni a wnawn yr oet 'we shall make the appointment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a · also a scribal slip wnawn i for wnawn ni (A pha beth a wnawn i? 'and what shall we do?'), the n of ni absorbed into the verb ending
__broaden__.gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel') · also soft-mutated after nyt oes in (nyt oes in gynghor 'we have no counsel')
__broaden__.gwisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun f. (gwisc hela 'hunting dress') · also 2 sg. imperative 'put on' (gwisc ymdan y gwryanc hwnn 'put on arms about this youth')
__broaden__.derw: daruot (darfod) — to happen; derw = deryw, the old 3 sg. perfect 'it has happened' (a chan derw yt dywedut 'and since it has befallen you to say'); the Red Book also writes derw · also in A derw ... wiscaw amdan y gwryanc 'has it come about ... to dress about the lad?', a slip for deryw, as the answer Deryw shows
__broaden__.geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on' · also soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'to' (y geissaw arueu idaw 'to seek arms for him')
__broaden__.allei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/she could' (hyt na allei dywedut 'so that he could not speak'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na · also soft-mutated (g lost) after the particle a (ef a allei llawer mab colli 'many a boy could lose')
__broaden__.eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend') · also 'life' (colli y eneit 'to lose his life')
__broaden__.uuost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were, you have been', soft-mutated after the perfective particle ry (ry uuost ti) · also soft-mutated after a fronted predicate (direidwreic uuost eiroet 'a wicked woman you have ever been')
__broaden__.dylyei: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, deserve; 3 sg. imperfect, negated 'would not deserve' (ual nas dylyei 'such that it would not deserve it') · also positive 'ought' (y rann a dylyei uot am y hwyneb 'the part that ought to be about her face') · also negated 'ought not' (ny dylyei neb uot yn borth it 'no one ought to be a help to you')
__broaden__.rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this') · also 'because of, against' (chwynaw yn luttaf rac Aranrot 'complaining bitterly about Aranrhod')
__broaden__.delediwhaf: telediw (no modern form) — handsome, comely; superlative delediwhaf 'handsomest' (yny oed delediwhaf gwass 'until he was the handsomest youth'); soft-mutated (t>d) as the complement directly after oed · also soft-mutated (t>d) after yn (ac yn delediwhaf guas 'and the handsomest lad')
__broaden__.gyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m., soft-mutated after y/a 'his' (y gyuoeth 'his realm') · also soft after o 'of' (o gyuoeth 'of realm') and as the object of a verb (phei mynhut gyuoeth 'if you wanted a realm') · also soft-mutated (c>g) after heb 'without' (y wr heb gyuoeth idaw 'to a man without a realm of his own')
__broaden__.lys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (parth a'y lys) · also soft after prif 'chief', which softens the noun it precedes (prif lys 'chief court') · also soft-mutated as the object of kyuanhedwys (kyuanhedwys lys idaw 'built a court for him')
__broaden__.wreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after a'y/possessive (ymdidan a'y wreic) · also soft after the article, as a feminine noun (y wreic 'the woman') · also soft after predicative yn (yn wreic 'as wife') and as the subject straight after a verb (ny bu wreic delediwach 'there was no comelier woman') · also soft as the object of a verb (na chaffo wreic uyth 'that he never get a wife') and in address (A wreic 'O woman')
__broaden__.heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay') · also standing without its subject (Och, heb, pa ryw dygyuor 'alas, said (she), what kind of muster')
__broaden__.y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach) · (14) y ar 'from off' (y ar seith cantref Dyuet 'from off the seven cantrefs of Dyfed') · also y 'its, his' before a verbal noun, standing for the noun's object and softening it (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'; na'y ollwng 'nor releasing it') · y hediw 'from today' (a blwydyn y hediw 'and a year from today'); y 'to' before a verbal noun of purpose (lle idaw y benelinyaw 'a place for him to recline'); y 'his' twice in ar y bwyt a'y llynn 'on his food and his drink' · also (15) 'their' (for eu) with h- before a vowel (y harganuot o'r gaer 'their being seen from the fort'; a'y hanuon idi 'and sending them to her'), the h- being the possessive's sign
